Each Pillar is an Anchor and bears one named binding: 1. Outer Heaven Pillar - movement, teleportation, flight, phasing, possession, and remote origins. 2. Meridian Pillar - Cultivation Point expenditure and recovery, Sphere techniques, weapon-delivered cultivation, and Domain Armament functions. 3. Core Pillar - Path, Subpath, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Foundation active systems, cultivated-item activations, Recorded Arts, Forged Techniques, and Immortal Arts.

Seal Pillar Profile: Size Medium object; AC Your Cultivation Save DC; Hit Points 6 x your CL each; Resistance Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from noncultivated attacks; Immunity Poison and Psychic damage; Source CL Your CL; Movement None.

Failed Save bindings: Within 2 CL or higher: Outer Heaven and Meridian Pillars. 3-5 CL lower: All three Pillars. At least 6 CL lower, Completely Subdued, or already bearing your Core Seal: All three Pillars, and Core Pillar imposes Complete Cultivation Suppression.

At the end of each of its turns, a target within 2 CL of you or higher repeats the Charisma save. On success, suppress one active Pillar of its choice until the end of its next turn. A target 3-5 CL lower repeats the save at the end of every second turn. A target at least 6 CL lower receives no automatic repeat save.

Binding Effects: Outer Heaven - Speed is 0; cannot willingly teleport, fly, phase, become Incorporeal, possess, or use a remote technique origin. Meridian - cannot spend or regain Cultivation Points, use Sphere techniques, weapon-delivered techniques, or Domain Armament functions. Core - cannot activate Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation active, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, cultivated-item, Recorded Art, Forged Technique, Immortal Art, or transformation features. When all three are active, the target suffers Complete Cultivation Suppression.

Break a Pillar: A Pillar ends when reduced to 0 Hit Points, lawfully displaced outside 60 feet of the target, or overcome by an equal- or higher-authority seal-breaking effect. A creature adjacent to a Pillar may use an Action to attempt a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. On success, deal Force damage to the Pillar equal to 5 x that creature's PB, ignoring resistance.

Sealed Passage: A creature or effect cannot teleport, phase, summon, or project through the triangle defined by the three Pillars when its Source CL is lower than yours. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check against your save DC.

gm_lines: Range: 120 feet. Duration: 1 minute.  Cost: 8 Qi. Limit: Once per scene.
Place five temporary Imperial Anchors in legal spaces inside the field. Each Anchor must: Rest on a stable surface. Be in an unoccupied space. Be at least 15 feet from another Imperial Anchor.

Imperial Anchor: Size Small; AC 16; Hit Points 4 x your Qi Cultivation CL; Damage Threshold: Your Proficiency Bonus; Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing; Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage; Source CL: Your CL; Radius: 20 feet.

Temporary Imperial Anchors: Do not count against your normal Anchor maximum. Project all five Circuit Modes. Are Connected to every other active Imperial Anchor. Disappear when the field ends. May serve as eligible Formation points. Cannot be moved outside the field.

Your normal Vein Anchors inside the field: Join the Imperial Network. Project all five Circuit Modes. Use a 20-foot radius. Gain the Imperial Anchor Damage Threshold. Retain their own Hit Points and AC.
Claimed Province: Half Cover against ranged attack rolls; Immunity to ordinary difficult terrain; Reduction to forced movement equal to 10 feet; Access to Dragon-Road Passage between active Anchors.

Hostile creatures in Claimed Ground: Treat it as difficult terrain. Cannot benefit from Dash after failing a Gravity Circuit save. Subtract 1d4 from checks made to break, suppress, or manipulate one of your Anchors.

Seal the Roads: Failed Save: The teleportation fails; The creature remains in its original legal space; The action, Bonus Action, Reaction, charge, or limited use is spent; Cultivation Points spent on the failed activation remain spent. A creature makes this save once per teleportation attempt. Does not block: Forced teleportation caused by you; Teleportation by an ally you designated; A Secret Law; An artifact or effect explicitly immune to spatial sealing.
Imperial Geomantic Command: At the start of each of your turns, choose two different Commands.

Harden the Mountain: Advantage on its next saving throw against forced movement.
Increase Gravity: Choose a 15-foot-radius area inside Claimed Ground. Until the start of your next turn: Hostile creatures treat it as difficult terrain. A creature saves once per turn.

While touching a stable surface, you sense the connected terrain and structure within 60 feet. You learn the presence and direction of: Significant hollows; Tunnels; Underground water; Major structural supports; Major structural weaknesses; Active Formation Anchors; Active portals touching the surface; Significant unusual spiritual pressure; A break or blockage in an active ley line; A cultivated effect directly altering the terrain.

Read the Dragon Vein does not automatically reveal: A motionless creature; A secret door that produces no structural discontinuity; Exact room contents; Written information; An inactive item; A concealed effect whose Source CL exceeds yours. You cannot retry until the effect changes, you obtain new evidence, or a new scene begins.

gm_lines: Limit: Once per scene
Emotional Pulse gains a range of 60 feet.
Use Emotional Pulse once during each of your turns without using an Action or spending Qi.
Emotional Contagion costs 0 Qi once per round.
Heartbreak and Heartmend cost 2 Qi instead of 4.
Weather of the Heart activates without cost and does not require Concentration.
Change emotional weather once per turn without using an action.

Master of the Inner Weather: When a hostile creature succeeds on a saving throw against one of your emotional features, choose one ally within 30 feet of you or the effect's origin. That ally gains one: Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus; Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; Advantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn; Advantage on its next saving throw before the start of your next turn. You may use Master of the Inner Weather once per round.

Emotional Reversal: Reaction, Trigger: An ally within 60 feet fails a saving throw against Charmed, Frightened, or an emotion-affecting feature. Add your Proficiency Bonus to the saving throw, potentially turning failure into success. Limit: Once per round.
Willing Heart-Shaping Rite: Outside a scene, perform a 1-hour rite with one willing creature. Cost: 5 Qi. The creature chooses one Heart Anchor and one Heart Release for the next 8 hours.
Deep Heart Anchor: After completing the 1-hour Rite, you and the willing target may continue for 7 additional hours and spend 10 Qi.

gm_lines: Choose one emotional weather when activated. At the start of each of your turns, change to another weather without using an action.
Allies you choose gain additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus on the first weapon attack or weapon-delivered cultivation technique they hit with during their turns (Weather of Rage).
Allies you choose gain Advantage on saving throws against Charmed and Frightened (Weather of Sorrow).
Allies you choose cannot be Frightened by a source whose Source CL is lower than yours (Weather of Fear).
At the start of an ally's turn in the aura, it gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus (Weather of Joy).

Allies you choose: Do not provoke Opportunity Attacks when moving 5 feet or less during a turn; Gain Advantage on the first saving throw they make each round against Charmed or Frightened (Weather of Calm).

Heartward Aid: Once during each of your turns, choose one ally inside the aura and grant one benefit: Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus; Move it 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; Advantage on its next saving throw before the start of your next turn; End Frightened when its Source CL is lower than yours; Allow an immediate repeated save with Advantage against a higher-CL Frightened or Charmed effect.

gm_lines: Move the Stones: Once during each of your turns, move one Stone up to 20 feet without using an action. The Stone: Travels along a visible legal path. Cannot pass through Total Cover, sealed Formations, or spatial locks. Does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Reassign Shape: Once during each of your turns, change one Stone's Shape without using an action.

Claim Territory: Action. Requirement: At least three connected Stones form a closed boundary. Duration: Until the boundary is broken, you claim another territory, or the scene ends. Cost: 3 Qi. The enclosed area becomes your Claimed Territory. You may maintain one Claimed Territory. Inside it: Allies you choose ignore difficult terrain created by your board. Allies gain +1 AC. Hostile creatures treat the area as difficult terrain. Hostile creatures cannot benefit from ordinary concealment against your awareness of their position. A hostile creature crossing a Board Line pays 5 additional feet of movement. Your Board features use any Stone on the boundary as their origin.

Territory Tax: The first time during each turn that a hostile creature inside Claimed Territory spends Cultivation Points, choose one: Increase the cost by 1. Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Move one Stone 10 feet. Move one ally inside the Territory 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. A cost cannot be increased more than once by Territory Tax during the same turn.

Take the Liberty: Reaction. Trigger: A hostile creature inside Claimed Territory destroys, suppresses, or removes one of your Stones. Limit: Once per round. Choose one: Place one temporary Stone in a legal space within 15 feet of the destroyed Stone. It lasts until the start of your next turn. Make a Cultivation Attack against the triggering creature. On a hit, deal 3d8 Force damage. The triggering creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Move one ally inside the Territory 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

Whenever you Place a Stone, choose one Shape for it. The Stone retains that Shape until destroyed or replaced.

Binding Shape: A hostile creature within 10 feet of the Stone must make a Charisma saving throw before it willingly teleports, becomes Incorporeal, phases, or crosses a spiritual passage. Failed Save: The movement or transition fails. Any action spent is lost. Cultivation Points and consumable costs are not spent unless the attempted feature says otherwise. Successful Save: The movement functions normally. A creature saves once per attempted movement.

Opening Shape: The first time during each turn that an ally enters a space within 10 feet of the Stone, it may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This movement can follow a Board Line.
Pressure Shape: A hostile creature starting its turn within 10 feet makes a Strength saving throw. A creature is affected by one Pressure Stone per turn.

Veiling Shape: The Stone and Board Lines connected to it become visually inconspicuous. A creature hostile to you must succeed on a Perception or Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC to identify the Stone or connected Lines before interacting with them deliberately. Crossing a concealed Line reveals that Line to the creature until the end of the scene.

Meridian Shape: When a hostile creature within 10 feet spends Qi or another Cultivation Point, mark it with Board Pressure until the start of its next turn. The next Cultivation Point cost it pays before then increases by 1. A cost cannot be increased more than once by Meridian Shape during the same turn.

Sacrifice a Stone: Reaction. Trigger: A creature within 10 feet of one of your Stones takes damage, fails a saving throw, or would be forcibly moved. Limit: Once per round. Destroy that Stone and choose one: Reduce the triggering damage by 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier. Add your Proficiency Bonus to the saving throw, potentially turning failure into success. Reduce the forced movement by 15 feet. Move the creature 5 feet to a legal space without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The source creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. Sacrificing a Stone is a deliberate loss of board position and is not refunded.

Suppress it until the end of your next turn if higher. On a successful save, the effect remains. A willing creature can allow the tear without a save.

Heart-Rewriting Rite: Ritual Time: 1 hour. Range: Touch. Cost: 8 Qi and appropriate ritual materials. Requirement: The target is willing, helpless, Restrained for the complete rite, unconscious, or contained within a Heart-Sealing Formation. Choose one Rewrite: Remove one Heart Aspect. Create one Heart Aspect. Redirect one defining emotion toward a new subject. Weaken one defining emotion by one grade. Strengthen one emotion by one grade. Create a permanent Heart Anchor. Seal one traumatic emotional trigger. Restore an emotion previously stolen by you.

An unwilling target makes a Wisdom saving throw at the end of the rite. If its Source CL is higher than yours, it has Advantage. If it is at least 6 CL lower, it has Disadvantage and does not receive automatic repeated saves.

Failed Save: The Rewrite becomes indefinite. It remains until: You willingly reverse it. A Heart, Mind, Spirit, Karma, Dream, or soul-healing effect whose Source CL equals or exceeds yours removes it. A breakthrough or profound identity event overturns it. The target completes a specific printed recovery condition established during the rite.
Successful Save: The Rewrite lasts until the end of the next scene.

Identity Limits: Rewrite the Inner Heart can profoundly alter behavior and relationships, but it does not automatically: Replace memories. Grant skills or knowledge. Change a creature's creature type. Rewrite a true name. Transfer a soul. Override a Secret Law or higher-authority identity Anchor.

Heart Scar: An unwilling target bears a visible spiritual scar detectable by Qi Sensing and relevant Mind or Spirit perception. A healer examining the scar learns: That an emotional Rewrite occurred. The Source CL. Whether it added, removed, redirected, strengthened, or weakened an emotion. It does not automatically reveal the original or new subject.

gm_lines: Steal the selected Aspect until the end of the scene. The target loses the immediate benefits and compulsions of that emotion.
You must know or reasonably perceive the emotion through: Speech or conduct. Insight. Qi Sensing or emotional perception. A prior Emotional Pulse. A Heart Anchor or Source Rule revealing it.

Successful Save: The target retains the Aspect. You learn: Whether the selected emotion is present. Its broad strength: faint, ordinary, strong, or defining.

Use a Stolen Aspect: Bonus Action. Spend one stored Aspect to choose one: Implant it in a willing creature for the scene. Gain Advantage on one attack roll, saving throw, or Cultivation Check directly supported by the emotion. Add your Proficiency Bonus to one Emotional Pulse save DC against the original creature. Grant Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus to a creature receiving Courage, Loyalty, Love, Joy, or Calm. Force one creature receiving Fear, Shame, Grief, Rage, or Hatred to make a Wisdom save; on failure, it suffers the matching Emotional Pulse failed-save result until the start of your next turn. The Aspect disappears after use.

Create a visible or invisible conceptual division. Choose one relation that cannot cross.
Division of Passage: Creatures and objects cannot physically cross. A creature attempting to cross makes a Strength or Charisma saving throw.

Division of Qi: Cultivation techniques, Cultivation Point transfer, Remote Technique Origin, Domain Armament control, and active Qi tethers cannot cross. A technique whose Source CL equals or exceeds yours may cross after its user succeeds on a Cultivation Check against your save DC.

Division of Sight: Vision, Truesight, visual divination, and line-of-sight targeting cannot cross. Blindsight, Tremorsense, or another sense crosses only when its physical medium remains connected around the division.

Division of Sound: Sound, audible commands, audible techniques, and sound-based communication cannot cross. Thunder damage can cross only if its Source Rule does not require sound transmission and its Source CL equals or exceeds yours.

Division of Space: Teleportation, portals, phasing, pocket-space access, summoning, and planar movement cannot cross. Equal/higher Secret or spatial authority requires a Cultivation Check against your save DC.
Division of Healing: Healing, Temporary Hit Points, condition removal, Cultivation Point restoration, and restorative tethers cannot cross. Self-healing on either side remains functional.

Division of Command: Companion commands, Formation control, Domain Armament commands, possession control, and summoned-asset orders cannot cross. Assets retain their last legal instruction or default behavior.

Move the Division: Once during each of your turns, move or rotate the plane up to 10 feet without using an action. It cannot pass through a creature. A creature in the new space chooses the nearest legal side.
Severed Crossing: A creature that forcibly crosses after succeeding on a save gains 1 Severance Mark.

Division of Cause and Effect: A hostile or beneficial effect originating on one side cannot affect a target on the other side, even when its physical projectile or visual manifestation crosses. This is the most demanding form. Increase its Qi cost by 2. A Source CL equal or higher may contest with a Cultivation Check each activation. Secret, Karma, Fate, Samsara, and conceptual effects are not automatically blocked; they contest normally.

gm_lines: Apply Severance Mark: Once per turn after one of your Qi-powered features damages a creature, object, Cultivation Asset, or active manifestation, apply 1 Severance Mark.

Minor Severance: Cost: 1 Qi; Limit: Once per turn. Choose one relation to sever until the start of your next turn. An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, apply the full severance. On a successful save, apply the lesser result.

Foot from Ground - Full: The target cannot benefit from Tremorsense, Earth Glide, rooted stance, ground-based regeneration, or a feature requiring contact with the ground. It has Disadvantage on saves against being knocked Prone. Lesser: It loses one ground-contact benefit of your choice until the end of the current turn.

Voice from Sound - Full: The target cannot produce audible speech or activate audible techniques. Lesser: Its next audible technique before the start of your next turn costs 1 additional Cultivation Point.

Hand from Weapon - Full: One wielded nonartifact weapon, shield, or implement falls in its space. A bound Domain Armament becomes inert until the start of your next turn. Lesser: The item's next attack or active property has Disadvantage or -2 to its save DC.

Sight from Target - Full: The target cannot perceive you through ordinary vision until the start of your next turn. Lesser: Its next attack against you has Disadvantage. This does not defeat Truesight, Blindsight, Qi Sensing, or another nonvisual sense.
Reaction from Event - Full: The target cannot take Reactions. Lesser: It cannot take a Reaction against you.

Technique from Delivery - Full: The target cannot deliver cultivation techniques through weapons, Domain Armaments, projectiles, talismans, or implements. Lesser: Its next weapon-delivered technique applies no rider beyond damage.

Shadow from Body - Full: The target cannot Hide through shadows, darkness, or ordinary visual concealment. Shadow teleportation fails. Lesser: It cannot benefit from Invisible against you until the end of the current turn.

Cultivation-First Scope: Minor Severance is not limited to the listed names when an equivalent relation is clear and no broader than one listed example. The effect must state the two sides of the relation, what function depends on that relation, the exact duration, and the save or authority contest. It cannot at CL3 sever a complete Path, soul, permanent identity, entire Sphere catalog, or all cultivation.

Eligible attributes include one movement mode, one Resistance, one Immunity (which becomes Resistance unless your Source CL exceeds the target by at least 3), Regeneration or automatic healing, Incorporeal movement, Invisible, one elemental tag or damage conversion, one sense, one weapon or item property, one aura or field-following property, one size increase/transformation trait/manifested limb, one Sphere, one Method benefit, one Golden Core Form, one Nascent Soul feature, one Domain Armament mode, one Foundation active benefit.
Major-System Severance and Restoring an Attribute rules.
Range 60 feet; Duration 1 minute; Cost 5 Qi.

Choose one visible or identified active connection. The creature maintaining the connection makes a Charisma saving throw. If no creature maintains it, make a Cultivation Check against the connection's save DC.
Failed Save or Successful Check: sever the connection for 1 minute. Successful Save or Failed Check: the connection is severed until the end of the current turn.

Eligible connections include concentration, summoner to summon, controller to asset, wielder to Domain Armament, possession, talisman, formation to Anchor, oath to witness, curse to victim, teleportation route, healing tether, command link, item attunement, Recorded Art medium, and field to moving origin.
Permanent Connection Cut: spend 2 additional Qi and 2 Severance Marks on its source against a connection 6 or more CL lower.
Range 60 feet; Cost 3 Qi.

Establish Incense Pavilion: Ritual Time: 10 minutes; Range: 30 feet; Cost: 5 Qi. Create a fixed ritual pavilion centered on a censer, altar, brazier, shrine, table, or similar Anchor. Choose three Pavilion Rites. You may maintain one Incense Pavilion.

Pavilion Anchor: Size: Tiny or Small; AC: 15; Hit Points: 3 x your Qi Cultivation CL; Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing; Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage; Source CL: Your CL. Destroying or removing the Anchor ends the Pavilion.
Rite of Restorative Fragrance: After completing a short rest inside, a creature regains additional Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus. A creature benefits once per long rest.

Rite of Cultivation Focus: After completing a short rest or Cultivation Session inside, a cultivator regains additional Cultivation Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature benefits once per long rest. This recovery cannot be recursively amplified by another Incense Pavilion.

Rite of Purification: Allies and invited guests gain Advantage on saving throws against Poisoned, Disease, Temporary Corruption, Smoke, gas, inhaled hazards, and supernatural fragrance. After a short rest, each may immediately repeat one such saving throw with Advantage.

Rite of Honest Reception: Allies gain +2 to Insight checks. A creature that knowingly states a factual proposition it believes false causes the incense to darken for an instant on a failed Charisma save. The fragrance does not reveal which words were false, the correct answer, omission, mistaken belief, opinion, or metaphor.

Rite of Spirit Audience: Active spirits, possession, curses, and spirit paths leave visible traces. Allies gain Advantage on checks to communicate with willing spirits. A hostile possessing entity has Disadvantage on its first save each scene against expulsion or revelation.

Rite of Veiled Gathering: Sound and scent created inside become indistinct beyond the boundary. A creature outside cannot identify speakers, words, or individual fragrances without entering the Pavilion, using a higher-CL supernatural sense, or succeeding on a relevant check against your Cultivation Save DC.

Rite of Dream Communion: A willing creature sleeping or meditating inside may share a controlled dream-space with up to your Proficiency Bonus in other willing participants. Participants can communicate, rehearse plans, share symbolic memories voluntarily, and experience up to 1 hour of subjective conversation during a 10-minute interval. Cannot compel disclosure or rewrite identity by itself.

Rite of Coercive Atmosphere: A hostile creature entering the Pavilion makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failed Save until it leaves: It cannot take Reactions, subtract 1d4 from hostile attack rolls, and it cannot knowingly violate a clearly stated rule of hospitality without first spending 2 Cultivation Points or taking 2d8 Psychic damage. Successful Save: It ignores the Rite until the start of its next turn. A creature saves once per turn.

Resolve each attack when you reach the relevant creature. On a hit: Deal normal weapon damage. A target larger than you by two or more sizes cannot be pushed or knocked Prone by this feature unless another rule increases your effective size. Iron-Rain Passage is one activation. Qi Technique Potency and once-per-turn riders apply once across it. A weapon-delivered technique applies to only the first qualifying hit unless expressly expanded.

gm_lines: It ignores one level of Exhaustion for determining penalties. It may activate a feature despite one blocked or suppressed ordinary meridian channel.
Opened Gate: When Open the Twelve Gates begins, choose one Gate (Breath, Motion, Clarity, Power, Endurance, Continuity).

Forced Circulation: A target may choose to activate one cultivation system that is sealed or suppressed by a Source CL no higher than yours; each time it uses the forced-open system it takes 2d8 Force damage and gains one Treatment Strain. At three Treatment Strain, Open the Twelve Gates ends, the target gains one level of Exhaustion, and the suppressed system closes again.

Closing Strain: When the feature ends, if the target used Forced Circulation or was reduced to 0 Hit Points during the duration, it cannot benefit from Open the Twelve Gates again until it completes a short rest or receives 10 minutes of medical treatment.

Gate of Endurance: It gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus at the start of its turn when it has none. Gate of Continuity: The first time during the duration that it would be reduced to 0 Hit Points without being killed outright, it is reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.

gm_lines: Choose three non-Secret Spheres to become your Curriculum Spheres.

Each Curriculum Sphere must satisfy all of the following: You have narrative access to instruction, a manual, a teacher, or a comparable source. It is legal for your Path or another rule explicitly permits your access. It is not a Secret Sphere. It is not a temporary Sphere borrowed from another creature.
For each Curriculum Sphere, record two eligible Curriculum Techniques from that Sphere.
An eligible Curriculum Technique must be one of the following: The Sphere’s base ability. A basic attack or basic utility expression. A Tier 1 talent.
Prepare Curriculum Technique: At the end of a long rest or Full Cultivation Session, choose one recorded Curriculum Technique.
Revise the Curriculum: Whenever you gain a Qi Cultivation level, replace one recorded Curriculum Technique with another eligible technique from the same Curriculum Sphere.
Replacing a Curriculum Sphere requires retraining, new narrative access, and the normal campaign training procedure.

gm_lines: A creature cannot conceal whether it understood and accepted a term through a non-Secret effect whose Source CL is lower than yours.
Place one Fulfillment or Breach Mark per creature per round without using your Reaction.
Spending an Oath Mark costs no Qi and may occur once during every turn, no more than once per turn.
Recorded Oath rewards and sanctions can affect a target anywhere in the field.

Heavenly Confirmation: At the start of each of your turns, choose one accepted obligation active in the field and one party to it. If honoring, grant one: Restore 3d8 + your modifier Hit Points; Restore 2 Cultivation Points; Grant +2 AC until the start of your next turn; Move 15 feet without provoking; End one lower- or equal-Source-CL condition that directly obstructs fulfillment.

If breaching, impose one: Deal 3d8 Psychic or Force damage; Remove 2 current Cultivation Points; Prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn; Move it 15 feet toward a required position or away from a forbidden one; Suppress the exact technique, item function, movement mode, or system used for the breach until the start of its next turn.
Final Witness: Once during the activation, choose one creature bearing at least four Fulfillment Marks or four Breach Marks. An unwilling target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Fulfillment - Failed or Willing, choose one: Fulfill one remaining ordinary payment, passage, protection, or delivery term through heavenly substitution when the required resource is present in the field; Restore all Hit Points and up to half maximum Cultivation Points; End one non-Secret oath, contract, restraint, curse, or suppression that the fulfilled obligation was meant to release and whose Source CL is no higher than yours; Grant Witnessed Authority for 1 minute.

Breach - Failed Save, choose one: Apply the Recorded Sanction at maximum effect without spending Marks; Suppress every technique and item function used to commit the breach for 1 minute; Compel return to one legal boundary, prison, employer, beneficiary, or place of surrender named by the obligation; Impose Complete Cultivation Suppression until the end of its next turn.
Successful Save: Fulfillment target receives half the chosen benefit. Breach target loses Reactions and Cultivation Points equal to PB until the start of its next turn.

gm_lines: When you spend a Fulfillment or Breach Mark, choose one additional effect appropriate to the recorded obligation. A creature can be affected by one Invoke the Clause effect per turn.
Released Burden: End one non-Secret Restrained, Charmed, Frightened, or oath-created condition whose Source CL is no higher than yours when fulfillment expressly releases it.
